explanation_en: A compound preposition meaning 'towards' or 'in relation to' someone, usually regarding behavior, attitude, or feelings. It is a highly elegant and precise way to express direction of attitude, equivalent to 'hacia' but specifically for interpersonal relationships.

examples.en_text: He has always been very generous towards his family.
examples.target_text: Siempre ha sido muy generoso para con su familia.

examples.en_text: The government has a great responsibility towards the citizens.
examples.target_text: El gobierno tiene una gran responsabilidad para con los ciudadanos.

examples.en_text: I feel immense gratitude towards my school teachers.
examples.target_text: Siento una inmensa gratitud para con mis maestros de la escuela.

examples.en_text: The director should show more empathy towards his employees.
examples.target_text: El director debería mostrar más empatía para con sus empleados.

examples.en_text: We must change our attitude towards the environment.
examples.target_text: Debemos cambiar nuestra actitud para con el medio ambiente.

examples.en_text: His behavior towards the guests was excellent during the party.
examples.target_text: Su comportamiento para con los invitados fue excelente durante la fiesta.

explanation_en: Uses the 'volver a + infinitive' construction, which means 'to do something again.' This is a very common and natural way to emphasize repetition in Spanish, far more common than using 'repetir otra vez.'

examples.en_text: I repeat to you once again that you cannot use your phone during the exam.
examples.target_text: Te vuelvo a repetir que no puedes usar el teléfono durante el examen.

examples.en_text: I'll repeat it to you once again: don't worry about the money, it's my treat today.
examples.target_text: Te lo vuelvo a repetir: no te preocupes por el dinero, yo invito hoy.

examples.en_text: Sir, I repeat to you once again that the store is already closed and you must leave.
examples.target_text: Señor, le vuelvo a repetir que la tienda ya está cerrada y debe salir.

examples.en_text: I repeat to you once again that I'm not angry with you, I'm just tired.
examples.target_text: Te vuelvo a repetir que no estoy enfadado contigo, solo estoy cansado.

examples.en_text: I repeat to you once again that you have to turn right at the next traffic light.
examples.target_text: Te vuelvo a repetir que tienes que girar a la derecha en el próximo semáforo.

examples.en_text: I repeat to you once again that you have to do your homework before watching TV.
examples.target_text: Os vuelvo a repetir que tenéis que hacer los deberes antes de ver la televisión.

explanation_en: A highly colloquial Argentine slang expression. While 'cagarse a piñas' literally means 'to get into a fistfight,' in this context it is used metaphorically to mean 'to work extremely hard' or 'to struggle intensely.' It is vulgar/informal, so learners should use it with caution and only in very casual settings.

examples.en_text: I worked my butt off studying all weekend to pass this physics exam.
examples.target_text: Me cagué a piñas estudiando todo el fin de semana para aprobar este examen de física.

examples.en_text: We worked our butts off to paint the whole house before the new furniture arrived.
examples.target_text: Nos cagamos a piñas para pintar toda la casa antes de que llegaran los nuevos muebles.

examples.en_text: My brother worked his butt off to finish the project on time, but in the end, he did it.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano se cagó a piñas para terminar el proyecto a tiempo, pero al final lo logró.

examples.en_text: You worked your butt off fixing that old car, but now it runs like new.
examples.target_text: Te cagaste a piñas arreglando ese auto viejo, pero ahora funciona como nuevo.

examples.en_text: The guys worked their butts off organizing the year-end party so that everything would turn out perfect.
examples.target_text: Los chicos se cagaron a piñas organizando la fiesta de fin de año para que todo saliera perfecto.

examples.en_text: I worked my butt off cleaning the kitchen after dinner; it turned out spotless.
examples.target_text: Me cagué a piñas limpiando la cocina después de la cena, quedó impecable.

explanation_en: A common idiomatic phrase meaning 'an entire lifetime' or 'all my life.' The addition of 'una' emphasizes the completeness and weight of the time spent. It is used to highlight long-term dedication or struggle.

examples.en_text: She dedicated a whole lifetime to scientific research and now she is receiving this award.
examples.target_text: Dedicó toda una vida a la investigación científica y ahora recibe este premio.

examples.en_text: My grandparents have been together for a whole lifetime and they still love each other like the first day.
examples.target_text: Mis abuelos han estado juntos toda una vida y se siguen queriendo como el primer día.

examples.en_text: Learning to play the piano perfectly can take a whole lifetime of practice.
examples.target_text: Aprender a tocar el piano de manera perfecta puede tomar toda una vida de práctica.

examples.en_text: It's not easy to move to another country after spending a whole lifetime in the same town.
examples.target_text: No es fácil mudarse a otro país después de pasar toda una vida en el mismo pueblo.

examples.en_text: In that library, there are books that my father collected over a whole lifetime.
examples.target_text: En esa biblioteca hay libros que mi padre coleccionó durante toda una vida.

examples.en_text: We have known each other since we were children; it is a lifetime friendship.
examples.target_text: Nos conocemos desde que éramos niños; es una amistad de toda una vida.

explanation_en: A very common set phrase meaning 'nowadays,' 'these days,' or 'currently.' It is used to contrast the present situation with the past. It is suitable for both spoken and written Spanish across all registers.

examples.en_text: Nowadays, almost everyone has a smartphone.
examples.target_text: Hoy en día, casi todo el mundo tiene un teléfono inteligente.

examples.en_text: Nowadays it is very common to work from home a few days a week.
examples.target_text: Hoy en día es muy común trabajar desde casa algunos días a la semana.

examples.en_text: People prefer to shop online nowadays because it is more convenient.
examples.target_text: La gente prefiere comprar en línea hoy en día porque es más cómodo.

examples.en_text: Nowadays, learning a second language is essential to find a good job.
examples.target_text: Hoy en día, aprender un segundo idioma es fundamental para encontrar un buen trabajo.

examples.en_text: Many young people worry about the environment nowadays.
examples.target_text: Muchos jóvenes se preocupan por el medio ambiente hoy en día.

examples.en_text: Traveling abroad is much easier nowadays thanks to cheap flights.
examples.target_text: Viajar al extranjero es mucho más fácil hoy en día gracias a los vuelos baratos.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'adrift' (like a boat without steerage), this idiom is used metaphorically to describe someone who is helpless, without direction, or left to fend for themselves in a difficult situation. It is highly expressive and common in literature and daily speech.

examples.en_text: The fishing boat was left adrift in the ocean after a heavy storm.
examples.target_text: El barco de pesca quedó a la deriva en el océano tras una fuerte tormenta.

examples.en_text: After losing his job, he felt a bit adrift and without clear goals.
examples.target_text: Después de perder su empleo, se sintió un poco a la deriva y sin metas claras.

examples.en_text: Without a strong leader, the research project is drifting.
examples.target_text: Sin un líder fuerte, el proyecto de investigación va a la deriva.

examples.en_text: We saw a small canoe floating adrift down the river.
examples.target_text: Vimos una pequeña canoa flotando a la deriva por el río.

examples.en_text: If we don't talk about our problems, our relationship will continue to drift.
examples.target_text: Si no hablamos de nuestros problemas, nuestra relación seguirá a la deriva.

examples.en_text: The country's economy seems to be drifting due to the current crisis.
examples.target_text: La economía del país parece estar a la deriva debido a la crisis actual.

explanation_en: A formal adverbial locution meaning 'as quickly as possible' or 'with the utmost brevity.' It is commonly used in administrative, professional, and journalistic contexts to request or hope for a quick resolution.

examples.en_text: Please send us the signed contract as soon as possible so we can start the project.
examples.target_text: Por favor, envíenos el contrato firmado a la brevedad para poder comenzar el proyecto.

examples.en_text: We apologize for the inconvenience; we will resolve your problem as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Lamentamos las molestias; resolveremos su problema a la brevedad.

examples.en_text: The doctor recommended that I get the blood test done as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: El médico me recomendó hacer el análisis de sangre a la brevedad.

examples.en_text: If you are interested in the position, please reply to this email as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Si está interesado en el puesto, por favor responda a este correo a la brevedad.

examples.en_text: I asked the apartment owner to repair the heating as soon as possible.
examples.target_text: Le pedí al dueño del apartamento que repare la calefacción a la brevedad.

examples.en_text: Students must submit the final report as soon as possible so they don't lose the scholarship.
examples.target_text: Los alumnos deben entregar el informe final a la brevedad para no perder la beca.

explanation_en: This expression is used to describe an action that happens suddenly, abruptly, or all at once. It is highly common in everyday speech and can be used as a synonym for 'de repente' or 'súbitamente.' It often carries a physical or emotional sense of a sudden impact or change.

examples.en_text: Winter arrived all at once this year and we had to get out our coats.
examples.target_text: El invierno llegó de golpe este año y tuvimos que sacar los abrigos.

examples.en_text: He was so thirsty that he drank the whole glass of water all at once.
examples.target_text: Tenía tanta sed que se bebió todo el vaso de agua de golpe.

examples.en_text: Don't try to learn all the vocabulary all at once; it's better to go step by step.
examples.target_text: No intentes aprender todo el vocabulario de golpe; es mejor ir poco a poco.

examples.en_text: When he heard the noise in the kitchen, he woke up suddenly.
examples.target_text: Cuando escuchó el ruido en la cocina, se despertó de golpe.

examples.en_text: We had to pay for all the car repairs all at once.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que pagar todas las reparaciones del coche de golpe.

examples.en_text: She decided to change her life all at once and moved to another country.
examples.target_text: Ella decidió cambiar de vida de golpe y se mudó a otro país.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means 'to go blank' or to suddenly forget everything, usually due to nervousness, stress, or stage fright. It is constructed with the verb 'quedarse' to indicate a sudden change of state. It is widely used in academic, professional, and casual contexts when someone loses their train of thought.

examples.en_text: During the driving test, my mind went blank and I couldn't remember the signs.
examples.target_text: En el examen de conducir me he quedado en blanco y no recordaba las señales.

examples.en_text: When the teacher asked him, his mind went blank and he didn't know how to answer.
examples.target_text: Cuando el profesor le preguntó, él se quedó en blanco y no supo qué responder.

examples.en_text: If your mind goes blank during the presentation, take a deep breath and look at your notes.
examples.target_text: Si te quedas en blanco durante la presentación, respira hondo y mira tus notas.

examples.en_text: I had the whole speech prepared, but when I went up on stage, my mind went completely blank.
examples.target_text: Tenía todo el discurso preparado, pero al subir al escenario me quedé completamente en blanco.

examples.en_text: Our minds went blank when they suddenly asked us to explain the project.
examples.target_text: Nos quedamos en blanco cuando nos pidieron que explicáramos el proyecto de repente.

examples.en_text: I hope my mind doesn't go blank in tomorrow's job interview.
examples.target_text: Espero no quedarme en blanco en la entrevista de trabajo de mañana.

explanation_en: The idiomatic construction 'pasarlo mal' (or 'pasarlo bien/genial') is the standard way in Spanish to express having a bad (or good) time. Learners often incorrectly translate 'to have a hard time' literally, but using 'pasarlo mal' sounds much more natural and native. The pronoun 'lo' is fixed in this construction.

examples.en_text: When I had the flu last month, I had a pretty hard time.
examples.target_text: Cuando tuve la gripe el mes pasado, lo pasé bastante mal.

examples.en_text: She had a pretty hard time when she split up with her partner.
examples.target_text: Ella lo pasó bastante mal cuando se separó de su pareja.

examples.en_text: We got lost in the mountains and had a pretty hard time until we found the path.
examples.target_text: Nos perdimos en la montaña y lo pasamos bastante mal hasta que encontramos el camino.

examples.en_text: I know you had a pretty hard time with the exam, but at least it's over now.
examples.target_text: Sé que lo pasaste bastante mal en el examen, pero al menos ya terminó.

examples.en_text: At first, my grandparents had a pretty hard time when they emigrated.
examples.target_text: Al principio, mis abuelos lo pasaron bastante mal cuando emigraron.

examples.en_text: I had a pretty hard time during the job interview because I was very nervous.
examples.target_text: Lo pasé bastante mal durante la entrevista de trabajo porque estaba muy nervioso.

explanation_en: This is a very common set phrase meaning 'in every aspect' or 'in all respects.' It is used to emphasize that a statement applies universally across all areas of a situation or person's life. It is highly useful for structuring arguments in both formal writing and spoken Spanish.

examples.en_text: The new employee is excellent in every aspect.
examples.target_text: El nuevo empleado es excelente en todos los aspectos.

examples.en_text: Living in the countryside has improved our life in every aspect.
examples.target_text: Vivir en el campo ha mejorado nuestra vida en todos los aspectos.

examples.en_text: This hotel is perfect in every aspect: the service, the food, and the rooms.
examples.target_text: Este hotel es perfecto en todos los aspectos: el servicio, la comida y las habitaciones.

examples.en_text: Since he started exercising, he feels better in every aspect.
examples.target_text: Desde que empezó a hacer ejercicio, se siente mejor en todos los aspectos.

examples.en_text: The project was a success in every aspect, thanks to the team's effort.
examples.target_text: El proyecto fue un éxito en todos los aspectos, gracias al esfuerzo del equipo.

examples.en_text: My brother and I are very different in every aspect, but we get along very well.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano y yo somos muy diferentes en todos los aspectos, pero nos llevamos muy bien.

explanation_en: This phrase comes from the idiom 'tener en cuenta,' which means 'to take into account' or 'to keep in mind.' It is formed with the verb 'tener' rather than 'tomar' (which would be a literal translation of 'to take'). It is widely used in both formal and informal contexts to show that you are considering someone's advice or a specific fact.

examples.en_text: Thanks for the advice, I'll keep it in mind for the next project.
examples.target_text: Gracias por el consejo, lo tengo en cuenta para el próximo proyecto.

examples.en_text: Your opinion is very important to me, so I will take it into account before deciding.
examples.target_text: Tu opinión es muy importante para mí, así que lo tendré en cuenta antes de decidir.

examples.en_text: We know the budget is limited, but don't worry, we are taking it into account.
examples.target_text: Sabemos que el presupuesto es limitado, pero no te preocupes, lo tenemos en cuenta.

examples.en_text: Tomorrow's exam is quite long, so keep that in mind to organize your time.
examples.target_text: El examen de mañana es bastante largo, así que tenlo en cuenta para organizar tu tiempo.

examples.en_text: I'm very glad that you are taking it into account for your final decision.
examples.target_text: Me alegra mucho que lo tengas en cuenta para tu decisión final.

examples.en_text: The bosses have reviewed your proposal and I think they have taken it into account for the new plan.
examples.target_text: Los jefes han revisado tu propuesta y creo que lo han tenido en cuenta para el nuevo plan.
